conventions.convention: Euclidean H1 consists of real W1,2 classes; H1_0 is the norm closure of compactly supported smooth functions. Boundary data are the quotient H1/H1_0, canonically equivalent to the fixed-atlas H1/2 space.
The anisotropic DN map is a real bilinear energy pairing on boundary quotient classes, with smooth symmetric uniformly positive-definite matrix coefficients.
For x=F(y), the conductivity pushforward is DF(y) γ(y) DF(y)^T / |det DF(y)|. Solutions transform by composition with F inverse; Riemannian metrics transform by pullback.

The uniqueness question uses dimension n≥3, a compact connected smooth manifold with nonempty boundary, a nonempty proper relatively open patch, and zero-frequency energy measurements with both inputs supported in that same patch. Orientability is not assumed.
The radial example assumes n≥3 and 0<ε<1/2; its nontriviality witness is the value (1+ε)^(2−n) I at the origin.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and Countable Choice, on a bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain of dimension at least two with nonempty boundary, Euclidean and fixed-atlas H1 spaces and their zero-boundary subspaces are boundedly isomorphic. The fixed trace has kernel H1_0 and induces bounded linear isomorphisms from both trace quotients to fixed-atlas H1/2.

Under AC, every boundary quotient class on a bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain of dimension at least two has a unique weak solution for a smooth symmetric uniformly positive-definite matrix conductivity. Its DN energy formula is representative-independent and a bounded bilinear form.

Under AC, a smooth diffeomorphism of the closed Euclidean domain with smooth inverse that fixes its boundary preserves the weak anisotropic DN map under the stated pushforward. In the Riemannian formulation, pullback preserves harmonicity and energy; fixing a measured patch preserves the stated local energy maps when the corresponding smooth Dirichlet solutions exist uniquely.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.1 writes the quadratic energies as integrals of γ|∇W|² and γ|∇u|². Here γ is a matrix, so those expressions are matrix-valued literally; the scalar energy used by the argument is (γ∇W)·∇W. The intended quadratic-form expansion and subsequent estimate are otherwise valid.

Proof 2.1 establishes equality of L2 traces and preservation of H1_0. Proof 3.1 then says, 'By step 2.1 its boundary class is f.' Equality of traces implies equality of quotient classes only after invoking ker T=H1_0; preservation of H1_0 alone does not establish that composition acts identically on the quotient. The required kernel result is available through the assigned trace-quotient lemma and the published trace-kernel theorem, but this inference is implicit.

Choice accounting calls the Riemannian pullback identity in steps 1.2, 2.2 and 5.1 'choice-free', while step 2.2 explicitly invokes the Countable-Choice change-of-variables supplier via AC and F11. The theorem assumes AC throughout, so its conclusion is unaffected, but the stated accounting does not match the supplied derivation.

seams_checked.note: Checked the scalar DN definition, fixed-atlas Sobolev definition and nonresonant regularity supplier against their uses here. Real Euclidean quotient data agree with the scalar convention through the assigned trace lemma; the manifold energy formulation uses the scalar γ=1 pairing and retains the connected, nonempty-boundary hypotheses needed for uniqueness. The prerequisite page makes no converse anisotropic uniqueness claim. The open-problem item explicitly qualifies the later manuscript's status rather than importing its conclusion. Historical survey passages were checked; retrieval of the cited 2026 manuscript failed, so its theorem and printed-formula descriptions were not independently verified in this review.
